coverage.identity_limit: Index units include reports, attachments, dividers and separately titled sections. This is not a claim that every original document boundary is knowable beneath redactions.

conventions: PDF pages are one-based physical page positions in the verified 704-page source.
pdf_pages is authoritative. start/end bounds are an envelope for non-contiguous documents, not ownership of intervening leaves.
null document_id means explicitly unknown identity/relationship; every such leaf has a stable unknown_unit_id.
Bates identifiers are visible transcriptions, not invented sequences. Bookmark names are recorded separately as metadata and can conflict with visible handwriting.
Printed page numbers, fax sequence numbers and Bates identifiers are separate fields. Null means no confidently visible number, not zero.
Exact markings retain legible text and case. Repeated label placement and typographic spacing may be qualified at page level; source images govern.
OCR excerpts and OCR files are navigation aids with known recognition errors, not certified transcriptions or reliable redacted-identity reconstructions.
All pages were visually inspected; dense transaction tables were reviewed for identity, extent and relevant evidence, not re-keyed or statistically replicated.
No document boundary was adopted from the prior partial register; the prior result served only as a question/source map.
Identical renders, including full-redaction leaves, are not automatically duplicates of the underlying records.
Supplementary Cella scan and Commission monograph are separate sources and are excluded from the704-page count.

IV. Conclusion

The Division of Enforcement has completed its investigation of trading in
securities to determine whether there was evidence that anyone who had advance
knowledge of the terrorist attacks on September 11 sought to profit from that knowledge
by trading in United States securities markets. We have not developed any evidence that
suggests that those who had advance knowledge of the attacks traded on the basis of that
information. In every instance where we noticed unusual trading before the attack, we
were able to determine, either through speaking directly with those responsible for the
trading, or by reviewing trading records, that the trading was consistent with a legitimate
trading strategy.

Introduction

In the aftermath of the events of September 11, 2001, and on September 17, 2001, when the New York Stock
Exchange (the “Exchange” or "NYSE") opened for business for the first time since that day, the NYSE initiated a
review of certain trading prior to September 11. On September 17, NYSE Market Surveillance staff received a call
from the SEC Division of Enforcement staff regarding the possibility that entities or individuals may have profited by
trading in certain stocks while having prior knowledge of the events that unfolded.

A Special Task Force was convened to conduct the investi

September 4 through September 10, 2001, to determine if any patterns emerged regarding execution of programs
restricted to these industries. Analysis did not reveal any activity that in and of itself warranted further review. The

(Morgan Stanley, UBS Warburg, Lehman, Goldman Sachs). Additionally, the programs would typically include
stocks beyond those stocks within these two industries. There were a couple of large trades executed by firms in
single stocks; however, these trades did not warrant further review as the firms noted had already been contacted
by staff for bluesheet information in those stocks.

Short Interest Review

Following the events of September 11, Market Trading Analysis analyzed the September 2001 Open Short Interest
figures on 47 listed issues impacted by the events of September 11, 2001. In addition to the issues reviewed by the
Special Task Force, other issues were included due to company inquiries and/or financial media coverage. Of the
47 issues that were the initial focus of this analysis, which included a review back to June 2001, the list was pared
down as follows:

1. Issues decreasing in value 10% or more between September 4 and September 10 and whose August
Open Short Interest figure increased by more than 10% were selected for further review (20).

2. Issues in the defense or security business secters that advanced in price on September 17 by 40% or
more were reviewed further (5).

other data, new account documents, account statements, contact names and telephone numbers, order information
and/or bluesheet intercase analyses, etc. The information was faxed or mailed to the SEC as received or, when

Specialist Surveillance

At the beginning of this investigation, staff, via the Member Trading Department (Specialist Surveillance) of Market
Surveillance, obtained information from the relevant specialists regarding unusual sales and/or short sales in
various U.S. airlines stocks during the period immediately preceding September 11. The information which
Specialist Surveillance gathered was ultimately supplemented by more extensive bluesheet information as well as
information about large unexecuted short sales from the firms which were bluesheeted. This initial information
assisted staff in identifying at an early stage those firms with significant activity in these issues.
